Subsampling custom-Stan sampling for an ordinal Markov random field

Source: vignettes/omrf-custom-stan-subsampling.qmd 
library(PDMPSamplersR)

The OMRF pseudolikelihood is a sum over persons. For person (n), each node is a categorical-logit conditional whose non-reference logits are affine in the threshold and interaction parameters. The subsampling observation is therefore one person, including all node conditionals for that person.

omrf_residual_envelope() specifies the analytic residual of a person’s gradient relative to a Hessian control variate at the anchor. For every grid cell, Julia bounds the residual rate of each person-node conditional along the trajectory with the categorical remainder bound, and sums these bounds per person. A person is drawn with probability proportional to its bound and accepted by thinning against its exact rate; no R callback runs in the event loop. Finite diagnostics below exercise the implementation, while the certified cell bounds are the guarantee.

Deterministic example and subset hook 

N <- 12L
P <- 3L
K <- 3L
X <- matrix(
  c(0, 1, 2,  2, 0, 1,  1, 2, 0,  0, 2, 1,
    1, 0, 2,  2, 1, 0,  0, 1, 1,  1, 2, 2,
    2, 0, 0,  0, 2, 2,  1, 1, 0,  2, 2, 1),
  nrow = N, byrow = TRUE
)
stan_data <- list(
  N = N, P = P, K = K, X = X, seen = rep(K, P), prior_only = 0L,
  prior_interaction_sd = 0.5,
  prior_threshold_alpha = 2,
  prior_threshold_beta = 2
)
prior_data <- stan_data
prior_data$prior_only <- 1L

stan_file <- system.file(
  "stan", "omrf", "omrf.stan", package = "PDMPSamplersR"
)
pdmp_subsample_hpp_path()
[1] "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/PDMPSamplersR/stan/pdmp_subsample.hpp"

The Stan source declares pdmp_get_subsample_size() and pdmp_get_subsample_index(). compile_pdmp_stan_model() installs the packaged header and the required compiler flags. Its thread-local buffer selects three execution modes from one persistent library:

  • an empty subset plus prior_only = 0 evaluates the full likelihood;
  • prior_only = 1 evaluates only the ordinary prior;
  • a nonempty subset evaluates the unscaled sum of those persons.

Julia applies N / m exactly once. The accepted selected gradient is retained for reflection, and every later proposal draws a fresh subset.

envelope <- omrf_residual_envelope(
  X = stan_data$X,
  seen = stan_data$seen,
  thresholds = "thresholds_0",
  interactions = "interactions_0"
)
anchor <- rep(0, 9L)
subsampling <- stan_subsampling(
  n_observations = stan_data$N,
  subsample_size = 1L,
  prior_standata = prior_data,
  residual_envelope = envelope,
  anchor = anchor
)

The same generic constructor works for another custom Stan likelihood only when it receives a certified residual envelope. The subset hook alone is an efficient selected-gradient oracle, not a proof of envelope domination.

Full and subsampling fits

The following managed check is disabled during routine vignette builds because it compiles Stan and runs replicated posterior chains. Set PDMPSAMPLERSR_RUN_OMRF_VIGNETTE=true to execute it. The benchmark driver benchmarks/omrf_subsampling.R contains the longer (N=200,500), (P=10,20,30) timing and ESS/second study.

run_checks <- identical(
  tolower(Sys.getenv("PDMPSAMPLERSR_RUN_OMRF_VIGNETTE")), "true"
)
compiled <- compile_pdmp_stan_model(stan_file)
mapping <- stan_parameter_mapping(compiled, stan_data)
stopifnot(identical(mapping$name[1:6], paste0("thresholds_0.", 1:6)))

edges <- rbind(c(1L, 2L), c(1L, 3L), c(2L, 3L))
person_loglik <- function(q, x) {
  thresholds <- matrix(q[1:6], nrow = 2L)
  interactions <- matrix(0, P, P)
  for (e in seq_len(nrow(edges))) {
    interactions[edges[e, 1L], edges[e, 2L]] <- q[6L + e]
    interactions[edges[e, 2L], edges[e, 1L]] <- q[6L + e]
  }
  result <- 0
  for (j in seq_len(P)) {
    if (x[j] > 0L) result <- result + thresholds[x[j], j]
    field <- sum(x * interactions[j, ])
    eta <- c(0, thresholds[, j] + (1:2) * field)
    result <- result - (max(eta) + log(sum(exp(eta - max(eta)))))
  }
  result + sum(vapply(seq_len(nrow(edges)), function(e) {
    2 * interactions[edges[e, 1L], edges[e, 2L]] *
      x[edges[e, 1L]] * x[edges[e, 2L]]
  }, numeric(1)))
}
full_loglik <- function(q) {
  sum(vapply(seq_len(N), function(n) person_loglik(q, X[n, ]), numeric(1)))
}
q <- seq(-0.2, 0.25, length.out = 9L)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  full_loglik(q),
  sum(vapply(seq_len(N), function(n) person_loglik(q, X[n, ]), numeric(1)))
)))

subset <- 5L
diagnostic <- stan_subsampling_diagnostics(
  compiled, stan_data, subsampling, position = q, subset = subset,
  velocity = seq(0.4, 1.2, length.out = 9L), flow = "ZigZag"
)
step <- 1e-6
explicit_selected <- vapply(seq_along(q), function(j) {
  plus <- minus <- q
  plus[j] <- plus[j] + step
  minus[j] <- minus[j] - step
  -(sum(vapply(subset, function(n) person_loglik(plus, X[n, ]), numeric(1))) -
      sum(vapply(subset, function(n) person_loglik(minus, X[n, ]), numeric(1)))) /
    (2 * step)
}, numeric(1))
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(diagnostic$selected_likelihood_gradient,
                   explicit_selected, tolerance = 2e-7)),
  diagnostic$selected_scale == N / length(subset),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    diagnostic$subsampled_gradient,
    diagnostic$deterministic_gradient +
      diagnostic$selected_scale * diagnostic$residual_gradient,
    tolerance = 1e-12)),
  max(abs(diagnostic$residual_gradient)) > 1e-4
)
for (flow in c("ZigZag", "BouncyParticle", "AdaptiveBoomerang")) {
  flow_check <- stan_subsampling_diagnostics(
    compiled, stan_data, subsampling, position = q, subset = subset,
    velocity = diagnostic$residual_gradient, flow = flow)
  stopifnot(
    flow_check$residual_rate > 0,
    flow_check$residual_rate <=
      flow_check$envelope_rate * (1 + 1e-10) + 1e-10
  )
}

anchor_check <- stan_subsampling_diagnostics(
  compiled, stan_data, subsampling, position = anchor, subset = subset,
  velocity = rep(1, 9L), flow = "BouncyParticle"
)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  anchor_check$subsampled_gradient, anchor_check$full_gradient,
  tolerance = 1e-10
)))

slab <- dense_gaussian_slab(
  0, matrix(stan_data$prior_interaction_sd^2, 1, 1),
  coef = "interactions_0"
)
common <- list(
  path_to_stanmodel = compiled, standata = stan_data,
  flow = "ZigZag", algorithm = "GridThinningStrategy",
  T = 300, grid_n = 15L, grid_t_max = 0.5,
  sticky = TRUE, can_stick = "interactions_0",
  model_prior = betabernoulli(1, 4), slab_prior = slab,
  show_progress = FALSE, materialize = FALSE
)
seeds <- 901:903
full_fits <- lapply(seeds, function(seed) {
  do.call(pdmp_sample_from_stanmodel, c(common, list(seed = seed)))
})
subsampling_fits <- lapply(seeds, function(seed) {
  do.call(pdmp_sample_from_stanmodel,
          c(common, list(subsampling = subsampling, seed = seed)))
})
replicated_summary <- function(fits) {
  run_means <- do.call(cbind, lapply(fits, mean))
  run_variances <- do.call(cbind, lapply(fits, function(fit) diag(var(fit))))
  run_ess <- do.call(cbind, lapply(fits, ess))
  runs <- length(fits)
  within_mcse2 <- rowSums(run_variances / run_ess) / runs^2
  between_mcse2 <- apply(run_means, 1L, stats::var) / runs
  list(
    mean = rowMeans(run_means),
    mcse = sqrt(pmax(within_mcse2, between_mcse2)),
    minimum_ess = min(run_ess)
  )
}
full_summary <- replicated_summary(full_fits)
subsampling_summary <- replicated_summary(subsampling_fits)
standardized_difference <- abs(full_summary$mean - subsampling_summary$mean) /
  sqrt(full_summary$mcse^2 + subsampling_summary$mcse^2)
stopifnot(
  full_summary$minimum_ess > 20,
  subsampling_summary$minimum_ess > 20,
  all(is.finite(standardized_difference)),
  max(standardized_difference) < 4.5
)
for (subsampling_fit in subsampling_fits) {
  counters <- attr(subsampling_fit, "subsampling_context_counters")[[1L]]
  if (is.environment(counters)) counters <- as.list(counters)
  stopifnot(
    counters$persons_evaluated ==
      subsampling$subsample_size * counters$analytic_residual_calls,
    counters$sampling_full_gradient_calls == 0L,
    counters$sampling_model_constructions == 0L,
    counters$sampling_data_constructions == 0L
  )
}

The analytic backend evaluates the selected person’s residual natively, so persons_evaluated is exactly m * analytic_residual_calls. initialization_full_gradient_calls records the anchor preparation; sampling_full_gradient_calls must remain zero. Likewise, the initialization model/data construction counts are fixed before sampling, and both sampling construction deltas must remain zero.
